incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: gpu-hotpath us-west-2 capacity_saturation detected. hotpath queue growth > 1200 reqs, 429s spike from 00:07UTC. Affected: hosted-api (text-gen), tier routing showing standard->hotpool overflow. dashboard: https://dash.redwood.example/s/cluster/us-west-2

alex: ack — i'm oncall. paging runs. collecting logs and current autoscaler state. any customer-visible reports yet?

tina: support: got two customer reports — PAYFLOW-1123 and CHATLY-998 both showing intermittent 429s and timeouts starting ~00:08UTC. tickets opened and owners cc'd.

priya: infra checking autoscaler. initial read: autoscaler heartbeat delayed and recent commit to rate-class mapping pushed yesterday looks suspicious. listing pool counts now.

priya: (command) ```
# autoscaler snapshot
hotpool-1: GPUs 48/48 (util 98%)
hotpool-2: GPUs 24/24 (util 99%)
dedicated-pool: GPUs 16/32 (util 50%)
queue_length: 1248
avg_latency: 2.9s
429_rate: 18% (up from 0.6%)
```

marc: runtime note: we saw a change to rateclass-to-pool mapping yesterday that moved some premium traffic to the standard tokenbucket tier by mistake. that makes tokenbucket units spend down faster under burst and triggers throttles even when GPU capacity exists in other pools.

sam: oncall-sre here — looking at tokenbucket controller logs. I see repeated rejected handoffs: `no_pool_match_for_rateclass: tier=gold -> pool=hotpool (not allowed)`. Looks like a policy deny during mapping resolution.

priya: confirming: autoscaler is healthy but allocation policy prevents moving some requests to dedicated-pool due to `tier_policy: strict_route` introduced in the last rollout. that created a hotpath choke.

alex: immediate mitigation options? can we 1) relax tier_policy, 2) increase tokenbucket refill for the affected rateclass, 3) spin extra GPs?

marc: quick wins in order:
1) relax tier_policy to allow fallback routing (low risk) — runtime flag flip
2) bump tokenbucket refill for `standard` so transient bursts don't hit 429s
3) temporarily route low-priority traffic to `dedicated-pool` or enable fallback model variant with smaller memory footprint

sam: i'm applying (2) now — patching rateconfig. will monitor 60s. command: ```
redwoodctl rate update --env prod --tier standard --tokens-per-sec 2500
```

deploy-bot: Starting rollout: redwoodctl/rate-config v2026.03.15-pt1 -> 8 nodes. CI checks passed.

sam: patched. observed token usage drop and 429 rate trending down. 60s window...

(priya): I'm changing tier_policy to `flex-fallback` to allow routing to dedicated-pool. Doing a controlled flip on routing layer. command: ```
redwoodctl router set-policy --env prod --policy flex-fallback --selector hotpath
```

deploy-bot: Router policy change started. canary 10% -> success. 50% -> success. 100% -> success.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: mitigation applied: tokenbucket bump + routing policy relaxation. 429s decreased to 4.2% in 3m, queue draining. Continue monitoring.

tina: updating customer tickets: told PAYFLOW and CHATLY we're mitigating and will follow up after stabilization.

alex: why did autoscaler not re-balance GPUs to hotpool earlier? seems like dedicated-pool had spare capacity.

priya: autoscaler didn't re-balance because allocation service respects `tier_policy.strict_route` when making placement decisions; that policy flagged the few premium keys as non-movable and autoscaler treated requests as unshiftable. It's a config-level policy, not autoscaler bug per se.

marc: root cause timeline: yesterday's infra rollout introduced `strict_route` to prevent noisy neighbor cross-pool routing. the change didn't include a fallback rule for saturated hotpath. under normal loads it's fine. under a surge, it blocked handoffs and tokenbuckets were exhausted -> 429s.

sam: logs snippet showing deny and subsequent 429s: ```
[00:08:12] allocation: deny route (key=acct:payflow) reason=policy.strict_route
[00:08:13] tokenbucket: tokens=0 -> reject 429 count++
[00:08:14] queue.len=1023
```

alex: status: queue now at 200 (was 1248), 429s ~2.1%, latency back to baseline for most traffic. good work.

tina: customer update sent: PAYFLOW-1123 updated. they reported reduced errors. keeping them posted.

priya: follow-up actions:
- revert strict_route rollout and add fallback in next patch (PR opened: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4521)
- add circuit-breaker to tokenbucket to avoid full depletion during policy-errors
- add alert for policy-change without fallback rules (monitoring rule)
- postmortem and runbook update for this failure mode

marc: I'll add a runtime check that prevents a policy flip that would leave any rateclass without a compatible pool under surge.

sam: oncall log: actions performed:
- bumped token refill for `standard`
- applied `flex-fallback` routing policy
- monitored queue drain and token usage
- coordinated customer comms
- handed off residual monitoring to priya for 02:30UTC watch

alex: handing off to priya for the next shift. summary: hotpath saturation due to `strict_route` policy + tokenbucket blowout; mitigations applied and holding. full postmortem required. priya — you're on for follow-up. :handshake:

priya: got it, taking over. I'll keep 30min checks for the next 3 hours and validate PR tests. Also will coordinate with product on rollout gating.

ops-bot: NOTE: runbook step executed: fallback-enabled, tokenbucket-bump recorded. Incident ID: INC-2026-0315-0789.

alex: thanks all. filing incident commander notes and tagging postmortem owners.

incident-bot: :memo: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. SLA impact: degraded (partial) for ~12m. Affected customers: PAYFLOW-1123, CHATLY-998. Follow-up: postmortem assigned to @marc and @priya.``
